correctness.rationale: Pollak rotation maps each circular preference sequence to exactly one ordinary parking function with an (n+1)-fold fiber, preserving luck and distinct favorites. At arrival i the three exhaustive classes have probabilities (N-i+1)/N, (i-1-M_{i-1})/N and M_{i-1}/N. They imply independent luck flags; conditional richness is stochastically monotone in each flag. Harris association proves nonnegative covariance of arbitrary increasing recodings, strictly positive for strictly increasing recodings by last-car pivotality for n>=2. Conditioning on the first i favorites gives Cov(L_i,M)=p_i(1-q^(i-1))q^(n-i), and summation yields n+2-(5n+7)q^n/2. Exact occupancy variances give correlation limit 0.63087856; uniform grid convergence yields Lambert-W(1) maximizer. Fresh independent direct parking enumeration for n=2..5 verified exact moments, all individual covariances and all threshold upper-quadrant tests. Finite tests do not establish all-n results.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks are restricted to explicitly stated bounds; infinite assertions rest on inspected analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The joint luck/richness transition, universal increasing-transform association, individual-car cross-covariances and Lambert-W location are distinct from known lucky marginal enumerators and species/richness marginals. Diaconis–Hicks Section 3 studies marginal luck and Section 4 identifies species of the circular model, but their displayed results do not provide the joint association or local covariance. A hidden joint generating-function corollary in older refined parking-function enumeration is an explicit priority risk.

value.rationale: Both luck (successful first choice) and preference richness (number of distinct initial demands) are canonical correlated statistics of random parking functions. The theorem determines the sign for every pair of increasing tests, not merely one moment, and quantifies location-dependent contributions and their scaling. This supplies substantive probabilistic structure that cannot be inferred from separate one-variable marginal formulas.
